title: The Big Sale
intro: An email from Meridu Store announces a sale. You are wary of every deal now.
But some messages are real. Mirage loves it when you stop trusting the honest ones.

p.text: autumn sale is on: up to 25% off lamps and desks
See it on meridu.store, or in the Meridu app.
Nothing to pay now. Shop only if you want to.

foot.text: You get this because you signed up to our emails. Unsubscribe any time.

addr.label: Shop's real address
addr.lens: It comes from news@meridu.store, the shop's real domain.
addr.why: A matching domain is good evidence. Scammers can sometimes fake it, so also look at what is asked.

subject.label: An ordinary subject
subject.why: Calm subjects are typical of honest mail.

name.label: Uses your name
name.why: It proves little, but it fits an email you signed up for.

deal.label: A believable discount
deal.lens: Up to 25% off, with an end date.
deal.why: Normal sales are modest. 80% off is the red flag, not 25%.

site.label: Go to the site yourself
site.lens: It sends you to the shop's own site or app.
site.why: Pointing you to the shop's real address is what honest shops do.

nopay.label: Asks for nothing
nopay.lens: No payment, no code, no login.
nopay.why: A message that asks for nothing is usually honest.

unsub.label: Says why you got it
unsub.lens: You signed up, and you can unsubscribe.
unsub.why: Honest senders say why they write and let you stop.

actions.label: Open meridu.store myself and look at the sale

go_ahead.line: The sale was real: lamps at 25% off, on the shop's own site, and nothing to pay until you chose to.

ignore.line: Nothing bad happened. It was a real message, and you stayed careful.

block_report.line: That was a real message. When every message looks like a scam, the real ones get lost too.
block_report.mirageSays: If you trust nothing, I win anyway.

what_if.block_report: It asked for nothing, gave a modest discount and sent you to the shop's own site. That calm is what real messages look like.
what_if.ignore: Ignoring was safe. Recognising a real message is the skill: it asks for nothing secret and matches something you know.

golden_rule: A believable offer that asks for nothing and sends you to the shop's own site is usually honest. Go there yourself.

quick_check.q: What made this sale email believable?

options.text: It had a sale in it
A modest discount, a matching address, nothing to pay or give, and it sent you to the shop's own site

quick_check.explain: Modest offers and no secret requests are the honest signs.

hints.nudge: What is this message actually asking you to do?

rows.k: A modest sale with an end date

rows.v: Go to the shop's own site
